title: Empowering Refugee Claimants and their Lawyers: Using Machine Learning to Examine Decision-Making in Refugee Law

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting claimant citizenship and nationality from refugee case texts using NER, predicting case outcomes, and applying post-hoc explainability methods (like SHAP, LIME, and Integrated Gradients) to measure token weights and identify inequalities in legal treatments.

Extracting claimant gender from refugee case texts, predicting case outcomes, and using token weight explainability analysis to evaluate correlation between gender features and asylum decision outcomes.
Extracting claimant age from refugee case texts, predicting case outcomes, and using token weight explainability analysis to evaluate correlation between age features and asylum decision outcomes.

Extracting judge names and tribunal identifiers from case texts and analyzing outcome predictions to detect systematic 'unwanted variability' (level noise/pattern noise) and biases between different decision-makers.
